sourceNote: Reused from fixtures/grading-calibration/mew-gold-star-back-whitening — the grading recalibration's own hand-verified anchor case (founder confirmed against the physical card, 2026-08-30). That case exists because this card has REAL, heavy, hand-confirmed physical wear: whitening along all four back edges and fuzzed/soft back corners, graded PSA 4-5. Genuine and heavily worn are not the same thing as counterfeit — this case exists specifically to check the screening prompt doesn't conflate the two. No backlit photo (grading capture is front+back only).
expectedFindings: edge_core_appearance and/or other wear-adjacent properties may reasonably note visible wear, but severity should stay at most 'minor' for ordinary handling wear — 'concerning'/'strong' would indicate the prompt is conflating physical damage with a counterfeit signal, which is the specific failure this case is designed to catch
notes: The highest-value case in this initial set: a real, damaged, unambiguously-genuine card. If this comes back with 'concerns found', the prompt is failing the exact distinction the design doc's risk register calls out (legitimate-variant / condition-vs-authenticity conflation) and needs rework before any known-fake cases are even worth testing against.
